outlook.statement: The Company is actively implementing rigorous plant-level cost-containment programs, enhancing preventative maintenance timelines to increase turbine uptime, and evaluating strategic capital allocations to flatten cash flow volatility. These operational enhancements and strict over-head cost controls are aimed at strengthening operational EBITDA margins and stabilizing net earnings over the upcoming 24 to 36 months.

Real GDP growth for 2026-27 is projected at 6.9 per cent. The Government's focus on scaling up domestic manufacturing in several strategic and frontier sectors announced in the Union Budget 2026-27, GST rationalization, promises well for India's maintaining the growth trajectory.

The Company continues to take steps for cost reduction, tight cash flow management, policy changes to mitigate the downturn. More wind mills which have outlived their technical life and continuing operation may prove uneconomical as tariff remains fixed for many years with no adjustment to inflation or factual cost of repairs and establishment costs have been retired.

Considering the huge outlay needed to achieve the targets set by the Central Government, only big business houses are jumping into the Green Power bandwagon as their pockets are deep and may be able to absorb the running losses in the RE Business which they may leverage against growth in their other core businesses. Further due to their size, they are able to negotiate better with utilities.

risks: Environmental variables (wind velocity, grid breakdown, and seasonal yield variations)
Historic low-tariff power purchase agreements (PPAs) restricting aggressive top-line expansions
Wind power has lost its bite due to pessimistic approach of many regulatory commissions and most State utilities
In many states tariffs have not been encouraging and sale to third parties are being discouraged by imposing high open access charges
State electricity boards have not been able to come to terms with renewable power due to its vagaries
Present environment in Green Energy is only for Big Players with deep pockets developing in terms of thousands of MW

Performance directly linked to Renewable Energy Policies of both Centre and State Governments, effectiveness of Nodal Agencies and formulation of encouraging policies by State Electricity Regulatory Commissions

Considerable delay in processing or decision making by state utilities and State Electricity Regulatory Commission and higher judicial authorities resulting in strain on sustainability of small wind farms and impeding future projects.

Inordinate delays in adjudication of matters by Electricity Regulatory Commission, Appellate Tribunal for Electricity and High Courts result in acute pressure due to huge mismatch in inflow and outflow of funds.
Delayed receipt of generation proceeds necessitates temporary borrowings to tide over mismatch, bearing finance cost.
Present environment in Green Energy is only for Big Players with deep pockets; many small and medium entities closing units.
Expenses are more or less fixed in wind power business.
